item.title: New immigration court tactic leads to huge lines and chaos in Miami
item.description: Chaos unfolds at the Miami immigration court after judges are assigned mega master calendars, hearings where judges see more than 100 immigrants at once.

item.title: Understanding the tech giants' oversized influence in American schools
item.description: Big tech companies like Apple and Microsoft use devices, training and conferences for teachers and students to embed in schools. The New York Times' Natasha Singer discusses the impact in Coding Kids.

item.title: Iran fires on its Gulf neighbors, retaliating for U.S. strikes after a monthlong lull
item.description: The six-month war has led to a spike in oil prices, roiled the global economy and posed increasing political problems for President Trump's Republican Party ahead of November midterm elections.

item.title: Greetings from the Royal Pavilion, a stunning reminder of India in southern England
item.description: Looking up at this 18th century building, it became clear the British didn't only bring their architectural style to India. They also took some of India's style home.

item.title: Chevron to expand in Venezuela, days after the U.S. and Venezuela strike oil deal
item.description: Chevron is the largest foreign oil operator in Venezuela. The deal will expand its footprint at a time of political and economic uncertainty for Venezuela.

item.title: Medical groups offer vaccine guidance to fill federal vacuum
item.description: In the unprecedented absence of federal guidance, leading medical groups are issuing their own recommendations for who should get the COVID-19, flu and RSV immunizations.

item.title: New lawsuits claim OpenAI execs put image ahead of safety in Canadian mass shooting
item.description: The suits say that recommendations to alert police about the alleged shooter were nixed by OpenAI's global affairs team, led by veteran political strategist Chris Lehane. OpenAI denies the claims.

item.title: Whatever happened to ... children infected with HIV due to failures in healthcare?
item.description: For years, Pakistan has seen cases of children infected with HIV due to unsafe treatment in clinics and hospitals. A current outbreak numbers hundreds of cases. Why does this problem keep occurring?

item.title: India's prime minister is wooing the Gen Z while cracking down on them
item.description: Over two months, protesters, most who appeared to be digitally-savvy GenZ, used social media to organize. Government's efforts to respond spotlight how the ruling party appears to be playing catch-up.

item.title: ICE says it now has enough body cameras. And, Congress averts shutdown before midterms
item.description: Immigration and Customs Enforcement says it now has enough body cameras to equip all of its agents. And, Congress votes to fund the government, averting a government shutdown ahead of the midterms.
